stage: Cached mechanism discrimination screen, not AP or training
question: Does removing the unavoidable adjacent-bin variance of DFL interpolation improve cross-view localization reliability beyond raw variance and geometric agreement?
distinction: Candidate24 scored fixed action likelihood under the native distribution and STOP remains. This tests a different property: cross-view ordering of actual native mean boxes using excess integer-support variance. It neither tunes that likelihood nor changes any stopped retrieval/fusion/training recipe.
hypothesis: For integer-support DFL with mean mu, the least possible variance is f*(1-f), f=mu-floor(mu). Subtract this interpolation floor, then normalize standard deviations by predicted width/height in native bin units. The remainder may distinguish localization reliability across view scales. This algebra is not by itself an innovation.
sample: Original candidate24 cached64 head-held-out train images, all five traces and original candidate18 owners. Same scene set has been examined repeatedly and was seen by the detector. No independent confirmation claim.
budget: Zero image decoding, detector forwards, fitting, or official evaluation. Read existing native distributions. AUC screen only.
construction: Normalize cached FP16 softmax to float64 sum1. Decode expected distances to boxes using cached anchors/strides and historical letterbox/windows, in float64. These reconstructed means are diagnostic coordinates, not asserted bit-exact FP16 raw boxes. Clip to original crop before adding offsets. Valid views require original available flag. No GT enters any reliability score.

scores.raw_variance: same formula and predicted dimensions, retaining all variance
scores.consensus: mean IoU to other available native mean boxes
scores.regret_agreement: IoU with frozen regret output, geometry-only strong reference

labels: Original GT owner only, candidate score>=.05, at least2 valid views. All unordered view pairs whose same-owner IoUs differ by>.01; symmetrize signed score differences and labels to remove arbitrary view ordering. Total pair weight per original row1. Tiny/small grouping from historical owner area.
pass_action: Only allow a newly registered matched low-cost learnability or fixed deployment screen, with raw-variance/geometry controls and unchanged stopped historical recipes. Need independent evidence and closer prior review before any novelty claim.
fail_action: STOP_THIS_DFL_QUANTIZATION_FLOOR_RELIABILITY_RECIPE. No threshold, normalization, coefficient, subset or variance-transform tuning on these results.
limits: One-to-many owner/view associations, dependent pairs and repeated train scenes. AUC is conditional ordering, not deployed AP or uncertainty calibration. DFL probabilities need not be a posterior of boundary uncertainty.
